gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: He answered all the questions with great ___ (CONFIDENT).
gaps.explanation: 'Great' needs a noun: confidence. 'Confident' is the adjective.

gaps.sentence: The campaign aims to raise ___ of road safety (AWARE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ness forms the noun: raise awareness is the fixed phrase; 'aware' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: The team played ___ and deserved to win (EXCELLENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'played': excellently (-ly).

gaps.sentence: We ___ the cost of the trip and ran out of money (ESTIMATE).
gaps.hint: judged it too low — that is why the money ran out (under-)
gaps.explanation: Running out of money shows the estimate was too low: underestimated (under- + estimated).

gaps.sentence: He ___ denied knowing anything about the plan (FIRM).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'denied': firmly. Note the doubled m before -ly.

gaps.sentence: Her answer was ___ , so we had to ask again (RELEVANT).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — it did not relate to the question
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'relevant' is 'irrelevant' (ir- before r). An adjective is needed after 'was'.
